summary: The root دمو (dmw) primarily refers to "blood." Its original form is debated, with evidence pointing to دَمَوٌ or دَمْىٌ, as seen in its dual and plural forms.
lane: دَمٌ دم [ Blood; ] one of the [ four ] أَخْلَاط [or humours ], (M,) well known: (T, M, K:) accord. to some, (Msb,) it is originally دَمَوٌ : (S, Msb:) or it is originally دَمًى ; (Zj, Mbr, S, M, Msb, K;) thus in the correct copies of the K; (TA; [in some copies دَمْىٌ , and in the CK دَمَىٌ ;]) though deviating from other words of the same form in respect of its pl. [which see below]; (Mbr, S;) as is shown by its dual, (Zj, M,) which is دَمَيَانِ , (T, S, M, Msb, K,) whereby [also] the letter gone from it is shown to be ى ; (Mbr, S;) but it has also for its dual دَمَانِ ; (T, M, Msb, K;) and some of the Arabs say دَمَوَانِ ; (S, M;) in which last, however, [accord. to ISd,] the و is substituted for ى , though generally و is changed into ى : (M:) and this original form is used by a poet, [namely, Hoseyn Ibn-El-Homám, accord. to one of my copies of the S,] in his saying, فَلَسْنَا عَلَى الأَعْقَابِ تَدْمَى كُلُومُنَا وَلٰكِنْ عَلَى أَقْدَامِنَا يَقْطُرُ [ And we have not our wounds bleeding upon the heels; but upon our feet the blood drops ]: (S:) or it is originally دَمْىٌ ; (Sb, T, S, M, Msb;) as is shown by its pls., (Sb, S,) which are دِمَآءُ (Sb, T, S, M, K) and دُمِىٌّ , (Sb, S, M, K,) also pronounced دِمِىٌّ ; (TA;) like as ظَبْىٌ and دَلْوٌ have for their pls. ظِبَآءُ and ظُبِىٌّ and دِلَآءٌ and دُلِىٌّ ; for if it were like قَفًا and عَصًا , it would not have such pls. (Sb, S.) دَمٌّ is ignored by Ks; but is used by poetic license; (M;) or it is a dial. var. of دَمٌ . (K in art. دم .) has a more special signification than دَمٌ , the two words being like بَيَاضَةٌ and بَيَاضٌ ; (S;) [i. e.] it signifies A portion of blood: (T, M, K:) or it is a dial. var. of دَمٌ , (M, K,) accord. to IJ. (M.) The dim. of دَمٌ is . (S.) [Hence,] رَجُلٌ ذُو دَمٍ A man seeking to obtain, or prosecuting for, [ the revenge of ] blood. (TA.) دَمُ فُلَانٍ فِى ثَوْبِ فُلَانٍ is a saying of the Arabs, meaning (assumed tropical:) Such a one is the slayer of such a one. (Ham p. 632.) الدَّمُ الدَّمُ وَالهَدْمُ الهَدْمُ , or وَالهَدَمَ الهَدَمَ , is a saying of the Arabs, meaning If thy blood be sought, my blood shall be sought; and if thy blood go for nought, my blood shall go for nought: or, accord. to the latter reading, as is said in the Nh, and where thou shalt be buried, I will be buried: or thine abode shall be mine abode. (JM in art. هدم , q. v.) See also an ex. voce دُمْيَةٌ . -b2- دَمُ الأَخَوَيْنِ [ The red, resinous, inspissated juice called dragon's blood; ] what is called العَنْدَمُ ; (S;) i. q. دَمُ الغَزَالِ ; (K voce مَظٌّ ;) now called القَاطِرُ الَمِكّىُّ ; or a species thereof; (TA;) [vulgarly قَطْر مَكَّة ; and also called دَمُ الثُّعْبَانِ ;] what is called in Pers. خُون سِيَاوُشَان (K.) -b3- دَمُ الغِزْلَانِ A certain herb, or leguminous plant, having a beautiful blossom: (M, K:) accord. to Lth, الغِزْلَانِ is the name of a certain herb, or leguminous plant, having a blossom. (T.) -b4- بَنَاتُ دَمٍ A certain plant, (M, K,) well known; (K;) a certain red plant. (T in art. بنى .) -A2- الدَّمُ The cat: (M, K:) mentioned by En-Nadr in “ The Book of Wild Animals. ” (M.)

headwords.def: دَمِىَ دم دمى دمي دمية, (T, S, M, MA, Msb, K,) [held by some to be originally دَمِوَ,] like رَضِىَ, (S, K,) which is from الرِّضْوَانُ, being thus [with ى ] because of the kesreh, (S,) [but most hold the last radical to be ى,] and دَمَى, (TA as from the Msb, [but not in my copy of the latter work,]) aor. يَدْمَى, inf. n.

دَمَّيْتُهُ دمى دمي دمية دميته دميتة, (S, M, K,) inf. n. تَدْمِيَةٌ, (S,) i. q., (S, M, K,) i. e. [ I made him to bleed; ] I struck him, or smote him, so that blood issued from him: (S:) [and I made him bloody; for] دَمَّاهُ signifies [also] he smeared him, or defiled him, or made him to be smeared or defiled, with blood. (MA.) Hence the prov., وُلْدُكِ مَنْ دَمَّى عَقَبَيْكِ, (M, TA,) Thy son is he who made thy two heels to be smeared with blood; (TA in art. ولد;) i.

استدمى استدمى استدمي He (a man) stooped his head, blood dropping from it; (M;) as also اِسْتَدَامَ, formed by transposition from استدمى. (Kr, TA in art. دوم.) استدمى غَرِيمَهُ (assumed tropical:) He acted gently with his debtor; as also اِسْتَدَامَهُ: (Fr, M and K in art. دوم:) judged [by ISd] to be formed by transposition from the latter. (M in that art.) استدمى مَوَدَّتَهُ He looked, or watched, or waited, for his love, or affection: [formed by transposition] from اِسْتَدَامَ. (M in art.

دَمٌ دم [ Blood; ] one of the [ four ] أَخْلَاط [or humours ], (M,) well known: (T, M, K:) accord. to some, (Msb,) it is originally دَمَوٌ: (S, Msb:) or it is originally دَمًى; (Zj, Mbr, S, M, Msb, K;) thus in the correct copies of the K; (TA; [in some copies دَمْىٌ, and in the CK دَمَىٌ;]) though deviating from other words of the same form in respect of its pl.
دَمَةٌ دم دمه دمة: see the next preceding paragraph.
الدَّمَى الدمى الدمي دمية, said to be the original form of الدَّمُ: see دَمٌ.
دَمٍ دم Bleeding; having blood issuing from it: (S, * Msb:) [and] bloody; i. e. smeared, or defiled, with blood: and signifies the same [in both senses]. (MA.)

دُمْيَةٌ دمي دميه دمية An image, or effigy, (S, M, Mgh, K,) of ivory and the like, (S,) or of marble, (M, K,) variegated, decorated, embellished, or coloured, (M, Mgh, K,) in which is redness like blood: (Mgh:) or an image, or effigy, in a general sense: (Kr, M, K:) accord.
دِمْيَةٌ دمي دميه دمية: see the next preceding paragraph.
دَمْيَآءُ دميآء, as in the Tekmileh; in the K, erroneously,, (TA,) Good, or good fortune, and prosperity. (K, * TA.)
دَمِىٌّ دم دمى دمي دمية [ Of, or relating to, blood; ] rel. n. from دَمٌ; as also. (S.) [In the phrase خ ما دمّى, in Freytag's Lex., دمىّ is a mistake for دَمَّى: see 2, last sentence.]
دُمَىٌّ دم دمى دمي دمية dim. of دَمٌ, q. v. (S.)
الدَّمَوِيَّةُ الدمويه الدموية دموي, meaning Hectic fever ( حُمَّى الدِّقِّ ) is a vulgar word of the dial. of Egypt. (TA.)

دَامٍ دام دامي: see دَمٍ. [And see the next paragraph.] دَامِى الشَّفَةِ, (M, K,) applied to a man, (M,) [lit. Having a bleeding lip, ] means (tropical:) poor. (M, K, TA.) شَجَرَةٌ دَامِيَةٌ (assumed tropical:) A beautiful tree. (TA.)

دَامِيَةٌ دامي داميه دامية, (S, K,) or شَجَّةٌ دَامِيَةٌ, (T, * M, * Msb,) A wound in the head that bleeds but does not flow with blood (T, S, M, Msb, K) as yet: (M:) such as flows with blood is termed دَامِعَةٌ. (T, Msb.) [See شَجَّةٌ.]

مُدَمًّى مدمى مدمي مدميي Red; applied to a garment, or piece of cloth: (M:) or anything in the colour of which is blackness and redness: (T:) [ of a dark red colour, like blood:] or anything intensely red: (S:) applied in this last sense [particularly] to a horse &c.: (S, K:) or, applied to a horse, of a sorrel colour ( أَشْقَرُ ) intensely red, like the colour of blood: (T:) or, so applied, of an intense sorrel colour: (M:) and كُمَيْتٌ مُدَمًّى of an intensely red bay colour: (S, TA:) or of…
مُسْتَدْمٍ مستدم Having blood dropping from the nose, while stooping the head. (As, S, K.) (assumed tropical:) One who draws forth his debt from his debtor with gentleness. (As, S, K.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
